title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 88
paragraphs: Cyrus was concerned by what Croesus had said, and he caused all the rest to withdraw and asked Croesus what he discerned for his advantage as regards what was being done. Croesus said: “Since the gods have given me to you as a slave, I think it right, if I discern anything more than others, to signify it to you. The Persians, who are by nature unruly, are without wealth. If, therefore, you allow them to carry off great wealth in plunder and to take possession of it, you must expect this result: whoever gets the largest share will rise up in rebellion against you. Now therefore, if what I say pleases you, do this: set spearmen of your guard to watch at all the gates, and let them take the things away from the men who are carrying them out of the city, telling them that the goods must first be tithed for Zeus. Thus on the one hand you will not be hated by them for taking away the things by force, and they on the other will willingly let the things go, acknowledging within themselves that you are doing what is just.”
